# Working in this repository

Axylo is a browser charting library. The product is specified in `docs/02-product-spec.md`; the build plan is `docs/03-plan-typescript-release.md`. Read the sections your task names before writing code.

## Rules for every change

- **Contracts are fixed.** `packages/axylo/src/core/contracts.ts` and `packages/axylo/src/public.ts` are the interfaces between modules. Do not edit them. If your work needs a change there, stop that part, finish what you can, and describe the exact change you need in your report.
- **Stay in your files.** Each task lists the directories it owns. Do not create, edit or delete anything else, including configuration and other modules. Several agents work in this checkout at the same time.
- **No runtime dependencies.** Use the platform (`Intl`, typed arrays). Dev dependencies already installed: TypeScript, Vitest, fast-check, esbuild, Playwright (system Chrome), axe-core. The network is not available; do not try to install anything.
- **No DOM at import time.** A module that needs the DOM takes it as a parameter or touches it inside a function. Pure stages (data, scales, formatting, layout, scene) must run in Node.
- **Hot paths use typed arrays.** No object per data point, no array of arrays per data point, no copying of large columns that the contracts say are borrowed.
- **Never guess silently.** Anything that cannot be drawn as given is reported through the `DiagnosticSink` with the code from spec section 3.5.
- **Tests come from the spec.** Expected values are derived from the specification and the fixture data, never by running the implementation and pasting its output. Use fast-check property tests for invariants ("for any data …"). A test you cannot make pass is reported as failing; do not weaken it or change its expected value.
- **TypeScript strict, no `any`** in exported signatures. `__DEV__` is a build-time boolean (true in tests).
- **Comments say why**, not what. Names are plain words.
- **Do not commit.** The coordinator commits.

## Commands

```bash
npm run typecheck      # tsc over the library, its tests, and the API examples in docs/api
npm test               # unit and property tests (Node)
npm run build          # packages/axylo/dist
npm run test:browser   # browser tests against the built bundle, in system Chrome
```

## Your report

End with a short report: what you built (files), what you verified and how (paste the last lines of the test run), what is not done or not verified, any contract change you need, and any place where the spec was ambiguous and what you assumed. Keep "ran and saw" apart from "expect".

docs/04-plan-performance.md:39:## 3. How to measure
docs/04-plan-performance.md:41:### 3.1 Metrics
docs/04-plan-performance.md:45:| Metric | Start | End | How |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:46:|---|---|---|---|
docs/04-plan-performance.md:47:| Time to first correct chart | The create call | The first presented frame in which the chart shows the fixture's data: readiness is signalled by the adapter (Axylo exposes a revision counter for this in benchmark builds), and the signal is validated on sampled runs against a screenshot compared with a reference | `performance.mark`, a `requestAnimationFrame` after readiness; screenshot sampling in separate, non-timed runs |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:48:| Main-thread task time | Same | A fixed settle window after readiness | Chrome DevTools Protocol `Performance.getMetrics` (task, script, layout and style durations). This counts work wherever the library schedules it: synchronous, microtask, timer or animation frame |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:49:| Update cost when streaming | First append | Last append displayed | Main-thread task time divided by updates; plus, per sequence number, the delay until the frame that displays it, the backlog, and the count of coalesced updates |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:50:| Frame pacing | – | – | Intervals between animation-frame callbacks, summarized per run: 95th and 99th percentile, and the count over 1.5 refresh intervals (25 ms at 60 Hz, 12.5 ms at 120 Hz). The refresh rate is recorded |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:51:| Input to display | A real pointer or key event dispatched at a known datum, timestamped | The first presented frame in which the readout shows that datum | A lightweight hook in benchmark builds, validated against Chrome traces on sampled runs. The Event Timing API is not used for this: it does not report `pointermove` or `wheel` |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:52:| Long stalls | – | – | Long Animation Frames entries, which report frames of 50 ms and more. Used for stalls only, not for the one-frame budgets |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:53:| GPU and raster time | – | – | Chrome tracing on selected headed runs |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:54:| Memory | – | – | Four separate numbers, never mixed: bytes in buffers Axylo owns (counted directly); JavaScript heap after forced collection (CDP); process memory including canvas backing stores (browser task manager figures via CDP where available); peak during a data replacement. Baselines: a blank page, and the page holding only the input data. Leaks: heap after 100, 300 and 1,000 create–destroy cycles following warm-up, gated on slope, plus a count of remaining listeners and observers |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:55:| Bytes | – | – | Minified, gzip and brotli size of each entry point from the packed distribution, CSS included; parse and compile time from a trace |

"Phone": one real mid-range Android phone, used at baseline calibration and at releases, when the device is available; when it is not, the result says so. |

docs/04-plan-performance.md:68:| Runnable combinations | Desktop × {Chrome, Firefox, WebKit}; Throttled × Chrome; Phone × Chrome. Nothing else is claimed. |

docs/04-plan-performance.md:98:## 4. The improvement loop
docs/04-plan-performance.md:112:| Order | Area | Why it is likely to matter |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:113:|---|---|---|
docs/04-plan-performance.md:114:| 1 | Work avoided: explicit invalidation, no relayout when tick labels do not change, simplification bounded by pixels and runs | The large gaps in Phase 1 were between whole configurations that did or did not avoid work. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:115:| 2 | Allocation in hot paths: typed columns end to end, reused buffers, no per-point objects | Streaming and hover run every frame. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:116:| 3 | Drawing command volume: one path per series, batched state changes | uPlot's approach; cheap to try. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:117:| 4 | Text: measurement cache, batched DOM reads and writes, reused label elements | 24 charts multiply every text cost. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:118:| 5 | Lookup: binary search on sorted x; a grid index for scatter that degrades gracefully on clustered data | Bounds hover and keyboard cost. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:119:| 6 | Partial redraw: a separate layer for cursor and focus | Removes full redraws from hover. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:120:| 7 | Startup: module structure, lazy code for zoom and the table | Affects every page. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:121:| 8 | Off-main-thread drawing | High integration cost; only if 1–7 leave a budget failing. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:122:| 9 | WebGL or WebGPU marks | Only if raster time is the measured bottleneck at sizes in the workload table. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:124:## 5. What makes a gain worth shipping
docs/04-plan-performance.md:128:| Condition | Rule |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:129:|---|---|
docs/04-plan-performance.md:130:| The gain is real and large enough | The lower bound of the 95% interval for the improvement is above the workload's smallest worthwhile improvement. Excluding zero is not enough. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:131:| The gain is perceptible or structural | It moves a workload across a budget, removes missed frame deadlines (shown with an interval over runs, not one frame in one run), or saves at least the workload's declared minimum in milliseconds. A percentage alone does not qualify: 5% of 0.1 ms is nothing. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:132:| Nothing else pays for it | No other tracked workload's interval shows a regression beyond its tolerance, in each browser where it can be measured. Inconclusive on a workload with a tight budget triggers a rerun, not a pass. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:133:| Bytes are accounted for | The size budget still holds. A change that adds more than 0.5 KiB gzipped needs a workload crossing a budget. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:134:| Correctness is unchanged | Scene snapshots identical, or every difference reviewed. All fidelity property tests pass, in particular F2 and F5. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:135:| Complexity is paid for | A new code path, mode or public option needs a workload crossing a budget or a gain at least four times the smallest worthwhile improvement. Otherwise the simpler code stays. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:139:### 5.1 Declared endpoints (provisional until the pilot)
docs/04-plan-performance.md:145:| Budget | Workload in the harness | Primary metric | Smallest worthwhile | Tolerated regression |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:146:|---|---|---|---|---|
docs/04-plan-performance.md:147:| P1 | `first`, fixture `trend` | Task time, median over runs | 1 ms | 0.5 ms |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:148:| P2 | `first`, 1 × 100,000 | Same | 6 ms | 3 ms |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:149:| P2 | `first`, 1 × 1,000,000 | Same | 25 ms | 12.5 ms |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:150:| P3 | `stream`, window 600 | Task time per update: one value per run (task time in the window divided by updates), median over runs | 0.2 ms | 0.1 ms |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:151:| P3 | Same | Runs with any interval later than 25 ms | Fewer runs with late intervals | No more runs with late intervals than the baseline |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:152:| P4 | `hover`, 1 × 100,000 | Input to the frame showing the matching readout, 95th percentile per run, median over runs | 1.7 ms | 0.8 ms |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:153:| P5 | `page`, 24 tiles of 340 × 200 px, fixture `trend` | Total task time, median over runs | 20 ms | 10 ms |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:154:| P8 | `compact`, 40 tiles of 160 × 48 px, one series each | Same | 8 ms | 4 ms |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:155:| P7 | `mem`, 1 × 1,000,000 | Bytes owned beyond the caller's columns | 10% of the two columns | 5% of the two columns |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:156:| P7 | `lifecycle` | Heap after forced collection, cycles 1,500–2,000 against 2,000–2,500 | n/a | Growth above 1% between the two windows |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:173:## 6. Catching regressions
docs/04-plan-performance.md:175:| When | What runs | Compared with | Action |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:176:|---|---|---|---|
docs/04-plan-performance.md:177:| Every pull request | Smoke set: W-first at 3×120 and 1×100k, W-stream at 600, W-hover at 100k, bytes. Chromium on a shared CI runner. | The merge base, built and run in the same job in balanced blocks | Screening only. A result worse than the workload's tolerance triggers one automatic rerun; two in a row flag the pull request. A size-budget breach fails it. Inconclusive is reported as such. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:178:| On flag, and nightly | Full workload set on the reference machine, runnable combinations from 3.2 | The merge base or previous night, and the last release, each rebuilt and run in the same session | Confirms or clears a flag. Opens an issue with the commit range for any workload outside its tolerance against the last release. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:179:| Cumulative drift | Each nightly also compares with the last release | – | Small regressions that each pass per-change screening are caught when their sum crosses the tolerance. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:180:| Before a release | Full set, plus Edge on Windows, Safari by hand, the phone profile when available, and all comparison libraries | Budgets P1–P7 and the previous release | A failed budget blocks the release, or the budget is changed in the spec with the measurements and a written reason. Never silently. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:181:| Quarterly | Comparison library versions bumped | – | Publish the updated comparison. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:187:## 7. Where Rust could be justified, and what it would take
docs/04-plan-performance.md:191:### 7.1 Candidates
docs/04-plan-performance.md:195:| Stage | Could Rust help? | Reasoning |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:196:|---|---|---|
docs/04-plan-performance.md:197:| Simplification and aggregation over typed columns (per-column extremes, binning, cumulative sums) at 1M+ points | Possibly | Tight numeric loops over contiguous memory; SIMD is available. JavaScript engines already compile such loops well. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:198:| Spatial index build and query for scatter at 1M+ points | Possibly | Memory layout control matters; no browser API involved. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:199:| Parsing large text inputs into columns | Unlikely | Strings must be copied into WebAssembly memory and decoded; the copy often costs as much as the parse. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:200:| Layout, ticks, label fitting | No | Small inputs; dominated by text measurement, a browser call. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:201:| Canvas 2D or DOM drawing | No | One boundary crossing per command. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:202:| Rendering to a pixel buffer or to WebGL/WebGPU from Rust | Only as a separate product decision | It replaces the renderer, brings its own text rendering, and does nothing for the DOM-based accessibility layer. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:204:### 7.2 Preconditions for starting
docs/04-plan-performance.md:211:### 7.3 Evidence required to adopt
docs/04-plan-performance.md:215:| Question | Evidence required |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:216:|---|---|
docs/04-plan-performance.md:217:| Is the workload faster for the reader? | The lower bound of the 95% interval for the improvement in the workload's primary metric is at least 20%, and the absolute saving is at least the workload's declared minimum, in Chrome, Firefox and Safari or WebKit. A function-level microbenchmark is not evidence. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:218:| What does startup cost? | Fetch, compile and instantiate time of the module, cold and warm, on desktop and throttled profiles, included in W-load and in the first render of the affected workload. Break-even stated for a page that draws one such chart once (cold) and for one that redraws it repeatedly (warm). |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:219:| What does data transfer cost? | Time and peak memory to move columns into WebAssembly memory and results back, included in the end-to-end number. If columns live in WebAssembly memory to avoid copies, the effect on `update`, `append` and P7 is measured too. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:220:| Where is the crossover? | The data size above which the Rust path wins end to end. It must be at or below sizes in the workload table. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:221:| Do small charts pay? | W-first at 3×120, W-page and W-load must not regress beyond tolerance, so the module loads lazily and only above the crossover. The byte, correctness and tail-latency gates of section 5 apply to the module as to any change. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:222:| What happens while it loads, and when it cannot? | `line()` stays synchronous. The TypeScript path draws until the module is ready; the switch happens on a later revision and is invisible. Tested: fetch failure, instantiation blocked by a Content Security Policy without `wasm-unsafe-eval`, `update` and `destroy` during loading, and a stale result arriving after newer data. In every case the chart is correct and no error reaches the page. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:223:| Does it run everywhere Axylo runs? | Script-tag build, Vite, webpack, Next.js. No reliance on threads, which need cross-origin isolation that embedded dashboards rarely have. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:224:| Are both paths the same chart? | Differential tests feed identical inputs to both and compare the selected source indexes, gaps, order and ties exactly, and floating-point results within a stated tolerance; the F2 and F5 property tests run on the Rust path; rendered output is compared within a stated pixel tolerance. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:225:| What does it cost to keep? | Recorded: the toolchain every contributor and CI needs; a native Windows build verified on Windows, not by cross-compiling; lazy bytes; CI minutes; lines of Rust; a named owner for rollback; and the permanent duty to maintain two implementations of one stage. |
docs/04-plan-performance.md:227:### 7.4 Decision
docs/02-product-spec.md:1:# Phase 1b: Axylo product specification
docs/02-product-spec.md:7:## 1. What Axylo is
docs/02-product-spec.md:15:### 1.1 Why someone would choose it
docs/02-product-spec.md:19:| If you would otherwise use | You get today | Axylo aims to add |
docs/02-product-spec.md:20:|---|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:21:| Chart.js | Simple API, permissive license, widest reach | Keyboard and screen-reader access without author work; reduced-motion support; a tooltip that appears wherever the pointer is; large data without expert options; a stated time zone on every instant |
docs/02-product-spec.md:22:| Recharts | The React default | A palette, a title, labels that fit, formatted numbers and dates without code; 100,000 points without seconds of blocking; the same chart outside React |
docs/02-product-spec.md:23:| Highcharts | The best reader experience of the ten | The same class of accessibility with no module to import and no commercial license; reduced-motion support; errors that name the field and the row |
docs/02-product-spec.md:24:| ECharts or ApexCharts | Many chart types | Fewer types, each of which fits its labels, reports bad data and is accessible by default |
docs/02-product-spec.md:25:| uPlot | The speed reference | Automatic sizing, a palette, bars and donuts without path builders, and an accessibility layer, at a speed the budgets in section 5 keep honest |
docs/02-product-spec.md:29:### 1.2 Who it is for
docs/02-product-spec.md:35:### 1.3 Principles
docs/02-product-spec.md:37:| Principle | In practice |
docs/02-product-spec.md:38:|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:39:| Correct before configurable | A default that can mislead (truncated bars, interpolated gaps, a silently dropped label) is a bug, even if an option fixes it. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:40:| Say it, do not guess | Anything Axylo cannot draw faithfully becomes a diagnostic with a code, a location and a fix. If values were left out, the reader is told too. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:41:| The data is the authority | Exact values, the table, keyboard navigation and descriptions come from the normalized data. The drawing is derived from it and may be simplified; nothing else may be. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:42:| Everything a reader needs is on; nothing else is | Title, units, legend, tooltip, keyboard, description and table are on. Entry animation, a marker on every point of a dense line, and decorative toolbars are not. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:43:| One way to do each thing | One logical data model, one method per kind of change, one place for colors (CSS). |
docs/02-product-spec.md:44:| The page is the theme | Font, text color and color scheme come from the page. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:46:## 2. Scope of the first release
docs/02-product-spec.md:48:### 2.1 Chart types
docs/02-product-spec.md:50:| Type | Variants | Typical question | Status |
docs/02-product-spec.md:51:|---|---|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:52:| Line | Multi-series, gaps; time, date, numeric or category x | How did it change? | 1.0 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:53:| Bar | Vertical, horizontal, grouped, stacked | How do categories compare? | 1.0 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:54:| Area | Single, stacked | How did the total and its parts change? | 1.0 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:55:| Donut | Up to eight slices | What share does each part have? | 1.0 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:56:| Scatter | Optional series | How are two measures related? | 1.0 (owner's decision) |
docs/02-product-spec.md:57:| Compact variant | Of line, area and bar: marks only, for KPI tiles and sparklines | Which way is it going? | 1.0 (owner's decision) |
docs/02-product-spec.md:65:### 2.2 Workflows
docs/02-product-spec.md:67:| # | Workflow | What it requires of Axylo |
docs/02-product-spec.md:68:|---|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:69:| W1 | Show a query result | Rows in, chart out; field types inferred where that is safe; bad rows reported. |

docs/02-product-spec.md:87:## 3. Acceptance criteria: the reader's experience
docs/02-product-spec.md:91:### 3.1 Faithful representation
docs/02-product-spec.md:93:| ID | Criterion | Verified by | Driven by |
docs/02-product-spec.md:94:|---|---|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:95:| F1 | Bar and area value axes always include zero. An author `domain` that excludes zero is widened and raises AX110. | Property test on domains, including all-negative and mixed-sign data; `bars` fixture (values 82–97) starts at 0 | R1 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:96:| F2 | Missing values are never drawn as zero and never bridged unless the author asks. An explicit `null` is a gap, silently. An isolated value between two gaps is a visible point. A missing bar shows a "no data" mark at the baseline, distinct from a zero bar; a slot a series merely has no row for gets no bar and no mark. On a time or date axis with a regular step, an absent step is a gap and raises AX105; `missing: 'zero'` on the field turns absent and null values into zeros for counts. Tooltip, table and announcements say "No data". | `trend` with nulls and `trend` with the same 7 rows deleted render the same gap; `dirty` fixtures; property test that no segment connects across a missing index | R5 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:97:| F3 | Input that cannot be plotted as given is reported, never guessed. The diagnostic registry (section 3.5) fixes each case's level, what is drawn and what the reader sees. | One test per code; the combined `dirty` fixture and the four one-bad-value fixtures yield exactly the codes listed in section 3.5 | R5, D5 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:98:| F4 | Three temporal types, never mixed silently. **Calendar dates** (`2026-02-24`, `2026-02`, `2026`) read the same in every viewer time zone. **Instants** (epoch milliseconds declared `type: 'time'`, `Date` objects, ISO strings with an offset) are shown in `timeZone` (default: the viewer's), with the zone named in the tooltip heading and the description. **Wall-clock times** (date-time strings without an offset) are shown as written, with hint AX112. Instants that all fall on the same time of day, whole days apart, raise hint AX111 ("these look like calendar dates"). A bare number is never assumed to be an instant. | Four fixture variants in UTC, America/Los_Angeles and Asia/Kolkata: (a) date strings: identical text in all three; (b) ISO strings with `Z`, (c) epoch ms with `type: 'time'`, (d) `Date` objects: each zone's correct local text, zone visible, AX111 raised; with `timeZone: 'UTC'` or `type: 'date'`: identical. Plus: both DST transitions, a leap day, an unparseable date | R3 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:99:| F5 | No smoothing. When a line is denser than the screen, the drawing is simplified with this guarantee: for every device-pixel column, and every contiguous run of valid samples inside it, the drawn stroke covers exactly that run's minimum and maximum. A break between two runs is always kept, even when both fall in one pixel column; a slot a series merely has no row for (weekly data beside daily) does not break its line, except inside a stack (F10). Stacked areas are simplified on their cumulative sums. Exact values always come from the data, not the drawing. | Assertions on which source samples the drawing kept, for: one outlier in 1,000,000; two peaks and a gap in one column; alternating valid and missing samples; tied extremes; device pixel ratio 1 and 2; several zoom levels. A sample that the drawing dropped is still reachable by keyboard and in the table | D8, D9 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:100:| F6 | Numbers and dates are formatted for the page locale. Ticks and readouts are formatted separately: ticks may be compact (`50K`); tooltip, table and announcements show the full integer part, and the fraction with up to six significant digits not counting the fraction's leading zeros (`123,456.75`; `0.000123456`; `0.1 + 0.2` reads `0.3`), with the unit. A custom formatter that throws falls back to the default and raises a diagnostic. | Expected strings for chosen values (large integers, small decimals, percentages, zoned times) in `en-US`, `de-DE` and `en-IN` | R4 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:101:| F7 | Domains follow one order of precedence: the zoomed view is inside the author's `domain` if given, otherwise inside the automatic domain. This rule is for value axes: the y axis of line, area and bar, and both axes of scatter. A continuous x axis of line, area or bar spans exactly its data and any x reference the chart draws (plus half a band for bars), so a time series is not padded to the next tick; so does a date or time x axis of a scatter, whose numeric x alone follows the tick rule below. After a zoom on x, a y axis with no author domain is fitted again to the values in view, by the same rules. The automatic domain contains all data, the reference lines and bands the chart draws (a compact chart draws none, so `reference` has no effect there and is reported as an option that does not apply) and stack totals, and ends at the first tick at or beyond each extreme (a compact chart draws no ticks, so its domain is the same one without being shown to end on a tick). A field declared `scale: 'percent'` (0–100) or `'ratio'` (0–1) ends at full scale only when its maximum is at least half of full scale and not above it. Nothing is inferred from a label. | Property tests; `bars` ends at 100 when declared `percent`; a 4% maximum ends at the first tick at or above 4% | R1 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:102:| F8 | Donut: slices keep the given order, start at 12 o'clock and run clockwise. The legend shows every slice's value and percentage as text, in slice order. A zero slice is listed without an arc; a `null` slice is listed as "No data". A negative value is AX120 and the chart shows its error state. With more than eight slices that have an arc (a positive value), the seven largest are drawn and the rest of those are grouped as "Other (n)", with AX121; zero and `null` slices never count toward the limit and are never grouped, so each stays listed on its own; the table lists every category. Shares are shown with at most one fraction digit. An all-zero donut shows the empty state. | `parts` fixture; one test per case | R7, landscape scoreboard 3.1, WCAG 1.4.1 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:103:| F9 | Up to eight series, no two share a color. Beyond eight, each series still has a unique combination of color and dash or marker (for bars, full and compact alike: color and fill pattern; for every chart type at least 32 distinct combinations, after which combinations repeat), and AX130 is raised. | Tests with 6, 8 and 12 series | R7 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:104:| F10 | Stacks place positive and negative values on their own sides of zero, and the axis covers both totals. The readout's total is the sum when every component has the same sign; when signs are mixed it gives the positive total and the negative total, the two ends the reader sees, not their net. A missing component is drawn with zero height and the stack is marked "incomplete" in tooltip, table and announcements. A component is missing whenever its series has no value at that x, whatever the reason: a null, an absent step, or a series that simply has no row there (a weekly series stacked with a daily one is incomplete on the days between its rows; the owner's decision, 2026-11-18: a stack must never show a total made of values the data does not contain). A stacked series' line follows its band, so inside a stack it is not joined across such a slot. | Property test on stacked geometry; mixed-sign and incomplete fixtures | R5 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:105:| F11 | Line, area and scatter are drawn in x order whatever the input order. On line, area and bar, two rows with the same x in one series are AX108 and that series is not drawn. On scatter, points sharing an x (or both coordinates) are ordinary data. | Shuffled `trend` renders identically; duplicate fixture | R5 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:106:| F12 | When a warning means values were left out or changed, the chart says so to the reader: a short note ("Values not shown: 2. See table.", worded so it reads correctly for any count) inside the figure and in the accessibility tree, in every build. | Production build given `dirty` shows the note | R5, R6 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:108:### 3.2 Legibility
docs/02-product-spec.md:110:| ID | Criterion | Verified by | Driven by |
docs/02-product-spec.md:111:|---|---|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:112:| L1 | No visible text overlaps other text or is clipped, and no label disappears without the reader being told. Remedies, in order: thin (time, date, numeric and `ordered` category axes only); wrap to at most three lines; rotate up to 45°; truncate in the middle, keeping every label distinct, with the full text in tooltip and table. If labels still do not fit, a visible note ("Some labels hidden. See table.") appears and AX143 suggests horizontal bars. Axylo never changes a chart's orientation on its own. | In a browser, as painted text and not in a model (in the engines of section 2.3 where results are recorded), after fonts load: for widths 240–1,920 px and generated label sets, zero intersecting text boxes (1 px tolerance), zero text outside the figure, truncated labels pairwise distinct. Repeated with the WCAG 1.4.12 text-spacing overrides, 200% text-only zoom, and a font that loads late | R2, WCAG 1.4.12, 1.4.4 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:113:| L2 | Text is at least 12 CSS px and at least 4.5:1 against what is behind it, including text drawn inside a mark and legend entries for hidden series. Marks, axis lines and focus indicators are at least 3:1. Gridlines are exempt: they are not needed to read a value while the tooltip and table exist. Holds in light and dark. | Computed-style and rendered-pixel checks in both schemes | R7, R10, WCAG 1.4.3, 1.4.11 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:114:| L3 | The chart follows its container with no call from the page, in both directions. With no definite height, the plot is 16:9, clamped between 160 and 480 CSS px tall, and the title, controls and table flow above and below it. A container that starts hidden or zero-sized draws when it gets a size. | Resize 720 → 360 → 720 px; hidden-then-shown test; `height: auto` container is stable over 10 frames | R16, D1 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:115:| L4 | Light or dark is taken from the chart element's computed `color-scheme`; if that is not set, from the luminance of the inherited text color. `--axylo-background` overrides both. Marks repaint within one frame when the scheme, forced colors, contrast preference, or the `class`, `style` or `data-theme` of `<html>` or `<body>` changes. Forced-colors mode uses system colors. | A page that sets `color-scheme`; a class-toggled dark theme without it; a light-only page on a dark device (must stay light); a runtime toggle; forced-colors emulation | R10 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:116:| L5 | A marker on every point appears only when adjacent points are at least 12 px apart (provisional value), and always for isolated points. | `trend` at 720 px has no marker on every point (A5's sparse shape markers remain); a 12-point line has them | R8 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:117:| L6 | Title, subtitle and axis titles with units are part of the chart. A value axis is titled with its label (the field name when none is given) and unit. An x axis that is a measure (number) is titled the same way; a time, date or category x axis is titled only when the author gives a `label`, since its ticks already say what it is. A reference line or band shows its label next to it. Axis titles never overlap tick labels. | Layout tests; `trend` fixture | R9, WCAG 2.4.6 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:118:| L7 | Empty data shows a message inside the plot area; so do loading, error and Axylo's own internal failures. No invented axis ranges, no blank box. A change of state is announced once, politely. | `empty` fixture: message visible and in the accessibility tree, no tick labels; forced internal error shows the error state | R6, WCAG 4.1.3 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:119:| L8 | When the figure cannot hold a readable plot (less than 120×80 CSS px for the plot), it shows the title, a short summary (the first sentence of the generated summary, on at most two lines, cut with an ellipsis beyond that; the full summary remains the figure's description) and the table control instead, and raises AX142. | Narrow and short container tests | R2 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:121:### 3.3 Interaction
docs/02-product-spec.md:123:| ID | Criterion | Verified by | Driven by |
docs/02-product-spec.md:124:|---|---|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:125:| I1 | Pointing anywhere in the plot shows what is there, by the picking rule for the chart type (section 3.6), within one frame at the 95th percentile. On line, area and bar the tooltip lists every visible series at the nearest x; a series with no row at that x reads "No observation", distinct from "No data". The tooltip stays inside the viewport, does not cover the active mark or any control, can itself be hovered, and lists at most eight rows plus "+N more". In a plot too small for it (decision 0004: narrower than 240 px or shorter than 140 px) the same content appears as text in a strip reserved under the plot; where even the strip would leave the plot under the minimum of L8, pointing highlights the datum without a readout and the values are in the keyboard reading and the table. Escape closes it until the pointer reaches a different datum. | Hover at 20 positions including all four edges; sparse-series fixture; narrow tile with eight series; Escape test | R15, WCAG 1.4.13, 2.4.11 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:126:| I2 | Legend entries that show and hide a series are toggle buttons with a pressed state, operable by click, Enter and Space. A donut's legend lists its slices (F8) and has nothing to hide, so its entries are not toggles and this row does not apply to it. | Keyboard and accessibility-tree tests | R12, WCAG 2.5.3, 4.1.2, 2.1.1 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:127:| I3 | Zoom on time, date and numeric x axes is reachable four ways: visible Zoom in, Zoom out and Reset buttons that work with single clicks; drag to select a range; `+`, `-`, `0` and Shift+arrows; and pinch when `zoom: 'touch'` is set. The wheel zooms only while the plot has focus, and never when Ctrl or Meta is held, so browser zoom and page scrolling are not intercepted. | Reach a given range by clicks only; by keyboard only; by drag; page scrolls normally with the pointer over an unfocused chart | D7, R12, WCAG 2.5.1, 2.1.1 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:128:| I4 | Every interaction works with a single pointer without dragging, and by touch. Every control is at least 24×24 CSS px. A one-finger drag on a chart scrolls the page (on a compact chart too: it takes no pointer input at all, C1). | Touch emulation; size checks | WCAG 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 2.5.1, 2.5.3, 4.1.2, 2.1.1 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:129:| I5 | First render is not animated. An update may transition for at most 200 ms. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` nothing transitions, on first render or on update. | After `document.fonts.ready`: first frame equals the frame at 2.5 s within a 0.1% pixel tolerance, in both settings; an update under reduced motion reaches its final frame in one step; a 24-chart filter change settles within 200 ms | R14 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:130:| I6 | A chart fed by `append` shows a Pause/Resume control. While paused, new rows are buffered and the view does not move. | Stream test | WCAG 2.2.2 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:132:### 3.4 Accessibility
docs/02-product-spec.md:136:| ID | Criterion | Verified by | Driven by |
docs/02-product-spec.md:137:|---|---|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:138:| A1 | Every chart has an accessible name: its `title`, or the heading named by `labelledBy`, or else a generated name ("Line chart of Sessions by Day") with AX140 raised in every build. The title's heading level is the author's (`level`), and it can be hidden visually. Every chart has a generated summary: type, series, x range with time zone, y range, each series' minimum, maximum and last value, and any omissions. `description` adds to the summary and never removes the zone or omission statements. Element ids are unique per chart. | Accessibility-tree snapshot for every fixture; a 24-chart page has no duplicate ids; axe `heading-order` | R11, R13, WCAG 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 2.4.6 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:139:| A2 | Keyboard: at most two tab stops while the table is closed, the plot and one toolbar with roving focus that holds legend toggles, zoom, pause and the table control. Every point is reachable in order; the series can be switched; the ends can be reached directly; focus can leave the chart. The focus indicator is at least 2 px and 3:1 and is not hidden by the tooltip. The exact keys and roles are fixed after the pattern spike in M1 (section 8). | Forward and reverse traversal in collapsed, zoomed, streaming and table-open states; focus after hiding the focused series; indicator contrast | R12, WCAG 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 2.4.11, 1.4.11 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:140:| A3 | Moving focus to a point conveys its text (series, x, value with unit, position) through the focused element's value text: the plot is a native range control whose `aria-valuetext` describes the focused point (decision 0001; earlier drafts said "accessible name or a polite live region", which the chosen pattern does not use, and A7 forbids announcements for navigation other than this). On touch screen readers, every point is reachable by swiping, or the table is reachable within two gestures. | Accessibility-tree snapshot after each key. No screen-reader rehearsal is part of 1.0 (the owner's decision, 2026-11-18): what a reader actually speaks on NVDA, VoiceOver or TalkBack has not been checked, and the conformance table says so. The script for such a rehearsal is kept in decision 0001 for when one is done. | R12, R13, WCAG 4.1.2 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:141:| A4 | "View as table" shows the data as an HTML table built from the normalized data when opened: the title as caption, field labels with units as column headers, x values as row headers, values formatted as in F6. It covers the current x range, 100 rows per page, with every row reachable by paging or by jumping to an x value. It sits in a focusable scroll region no taller than the plot, and opening it does not move other charts. | Table content compared with fixture data, including a value near row 900,000 of 1,000,000; a 24-chart page layout test | R13, WCAG 1.3.1, 1.3.2, 3.3.1 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:142:| A5 | Series are never distinguished by color alone, in any mode. Each line and area carries a shape marker at its last point and at sparse intervals, repeated in the legend and tooltip; under `prefers-contrast: more` or forced colors, lines also differ by dash. Adjacent filled marks (slices, stacked segments) are separated by at least 1 px of background. Bars are told apart by position and order, and by the legend and tooltip that name them; a compact chart has neither, so there neighbouring bar series also differ by fill pattern (series further apart may share a pattern: four patterns exist). The default palette has eight colors, each at least 3:1 on the default light and dark backgrounds, with a minimum pairwise OKLab difference of 0.10 (provisional) under normal vision and simulated protanopia, deuteranopia and tritanopia. On any other background, Axylo measures the palette against the resolved background and raises AX141 below 3:1. | Palette script scoring the rendered marks of an eight-series chart in both schemes, repeats included; rendered-pixel checks of separators; a grayscale screenshot in which three crossing lines can be told apart by marker | R7, WCAG 1.4.1, 1.4.11 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:143:| A6 | Content reflows at 320 CSS px and 400% zoom without two-dimensional scrolling. User text-spacing overrides do not clip text. | Viewport and style-override tests in three engines | WCAG 1.4.10, 1.4.12 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:144:| A7 | Data arriving does not speak. Announcements happen only for the reader's own navigation, and for a change of state (L7). While data streams, keyboard focus stays on the same datum until it leaves the window. | Stream test counting live-region changes with and without focus; 24 concurrent streams | R12 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:145:| A8 | axe-core reports no violations on any fixture in any state, including `heading-order` and `scrollable-region-focusable`. | CI | R11 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:146:| A9 | A conformance table lists every applicable WCAG 2.2 AA success criterion, the test that covers it, and what the author must supply (a meaningful title or `labelledBy`, series names, units, the page's own structure). It also states the limits in section 3.8. The criteria are the ones cited as "WCAG x.y.z" in the last column of this document's criterion rows; a criterion of WCAG 2.2 A or AA that no row cites is listed in the table as not covered by a test, with a word on why: not applicable to a chart component, the page's responsibility, or not assessed (it can apply to a chart, and no test is cited for it; the table claims nothing about it). | Published with each release; a CI check that every listed test exists | R11 |
docs/02-product-spec.md:147:| A10 | Every built-in string can be replaced through `messages`. Built-in English text is marked `lang="en"` when the document language is not English. | Test on a `lang="de"` page | WCAG 3.1.2 |

docs/02-product-spec.md:165:| AX110 | Warning | An author domain on bar or area excluded zero | Domain widened to zero |
docs/02-product-spec.md:166:| AX111 | Hint | Instants look like calendar dates | As instants, zone shown |
docs/02-product-spec.md:167:| AX112 | Hint | Date-time strings have no offset | As written |
docs/02-product-spec.md:168:| AX120 | Error | Negative donut value | Error state |

docs/02-product-spec.md:172:| AX141 | Warning | Palette below 3:1 on the resolved background | As themed |

docs/02-product-spec.md:176:| AX151 | Warning | `append` rows out of order | Accepted through the slower full update |
docs/02-product-spec.md:177:| AX131 | Hint | A compact chart has more than one series | Drawn, with dash differences |
docs/02-product-spec.md:178:| AX132 | Hint | More bars than pixels along the category axis | Drawn; the message suggests aggregating |

docs/02-product-spec.md:189:### 3.6 Type matrix
docs/02-product-spec.md:191:| | Line | Area | Bar | Donut | Scatter |
docs/02-product-spec.md:192:|---|---|---|---|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:193:| Picking by pointer | Nearest x | Nearest x | The band under the pointer | The slice under the pointer | Nearest point within 24 px; ties go to the later row |

docs/02-product-spec.md:257:## 6. Decisions and the findings behind them

docs/02-product-spec.md:262:|---|---|---|
docs/02-product-spec.md:263:| Diagnostics are a first-class feature with codes | R5: none of the ten named the field, the row or the problem. | Kept. Severity and delivery rewritten (3.5): readers are told too, and production builds are not silent. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:264:| Calendar dates, instants and wall-clock times are different types | R3: given instants, six libraries show a daily value on a different day in some zones, which is correct for instants and wrong for dates; given date strings, most of them get it right. The gap is that nothing says which one the author meant. | Kept, sharpened. The test now separates the types, and a hint fires when instants look like dates. Default zone for instants: the viewer's, with the zone always visible. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:265:| Accessibility is in the core, on by default | R11–R13. | Kept. The table is built on demand, not eagerly. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:266:| The normalized data, not the drawing, is the source for values, table, keyboard and summary | Reviews: a simplified drawing cannot return the values it dropped. | New. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:267:| No animation on first render | Reading starts at first paint, and with 24 charts loading at once motion competes with it. R14: four of seven animating libraries ignore reduced motion. | Kept, with the rationale restated. Update transitions stay capped at 200 ms. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:268:| Label fitting is a tested invariant with a visible fallback | R2. | Changed. The absolute "everything always fits" was infeasible in a 240 px tile; it is now "nothing overlaps, and nothing disappears without the reader being told". Rotation comes before truncation. |

docs/02-product-spec.md:276:| Chart types | Judgment, then the owner's decision. | All five in 1.0, plus the compact variant (3.7). |
docs/02-product-spec.md:277:| MIT, including zoom and accessibility | D7. | Kept. |
docs/02-product-spec.md:278:| React adapter in 1.0 | Recharts leads npm installs among chart-level libraries. | Built early to test the core API, reviewed twice, then removed from 1.0 by the owner on 2026-11-18 to keep the first release plain TypeScript. docs/02-product-spec.md:280:| Zero runtime dependencies | D4. | Kept provisionally; time-zone arithmetic uses `Intl`. |

The pair measures removal of the Canvas renderer, switch and Canvas-only styles with the shared renderer interface preserved. The SVG-only size snapshot uses artifact `20261122T055902Z-298b29e8-2e262a`, source hash `a57a243060881691`, before the startup optimizations. [Before removal](../../bench/results/size-before-svg-2026-11-22.json) · [After removal](../../bench/results/size-svg-contract-2026-11-22.json)
    14	
    15	## Historical M1 review and measurements
    16	
    17	The table below is kept as measured. These statements made from it in the first version are withdrawn or narrowed:
    18	
    19	- **Withdrawn: "nothing measured favours canvas except all-thread CPU during resize."** The recorded heap, DOM-node and layout counts also favour canvas.
    20	- **Withdrawn: the resize CPU gap is raster work.** The number is CPU for the whole renderer process; no stage was traced.
    21	- **Withdrawn: simplification bounds every chart by its width.** It was shown for line series only; point marks and many-series charts were not measured.
    22	- **Withdrawn: an SVG theme change needs no run-time work.** Both renderers recorded six DOM mutations per toggle; "no canvas drawing call" is all that was observed.
    23	- **Withdrawn: normalization and garbage collection explain the gap to uPlot.** About 71–73% of busy time in the production profiles is unmapped; the normalization share comes from development builds. It is a hypothesis to test, not a finding.
    24	- **Narrowed: "half the renderer memory."** The halving is of the increase above a data-only page at pixel ratio 2 (34.2 → 17.7 MiB). Absolute renderer memory was 74.7 → 56.2 MiB, and at pixel ratio 1 the increase was 23.1 → 18.4 MiB.
    25	- **Narrowed: "no frame later than 25 ms."** True of the recorded animation-frame callbacks; the window can miss an interval that spans its boundary, and a callback is not a presented frame.
    26	- **Void: every 24-chart page row** (page at pixel ratio 1 and 2, resize of the 24-chart page, and the memory row). The harness fix pass found that these runs drew no marks: at 230 × 115 px each tile is below the 120 × 80 px plot minimum of spec L8, so every chart showed its text fallback. The SVG records carry `svgPaths: 0`; the canvas runs held empty canvases. The numbers compare two empty charts and say nothing about the renderers. The harness now rejects a run whose chart drew no marks, and the page workload uses 340 × 200 px tiles.
    27	- **Narrowed: verdicts.** 149 metric comparisons were judged without adjustment for choosing among them, on six pairs or fewer per workload, with noise bands from one session and two workload shapes. Two "SVG lower" rows allow a gain as small as 0.16 ms (10,000 points) and 6.3 ms (dashboard at pixel ratio 2).
    28	
    29	Evidence: [bench/results/m1-renderer-comparison.md](../../bench/results/m1-renderer-comparison.md). One session of 39 runs, production build, headless Chrome 157, machine under load from other work, A-versus-A noise bands for two workloads only.
    30	
    31	### What M1 measured
    32	
    33	Canvas → SVG, medians of main-thread task time unless stated. "Lower" means the 95% interval cleared zero and the noise band where one existed.
    34	
    35	| Workload | Canvas | SVG | Verdict |
    36	|---|---|---|---|
    37	| Streaming, per update | 2.26 ms | 1.45 ms | SVG lower |
    38	| Theme change, per toggle | 2.68 ms and 27 drawing calls | 2.01 ms and no drawing call | SVG lower |
    39	| Resize, one chart of 100,000 points | 915 ms | 472 ms | SVG lower on the main thread |
    40	| Same, CPU across all threads | 1,035 ms | 1,770 ms | **SVG higher** |
    41	| Resize, 24-chart page | 730 ms | 525 ms | Void: no marks were drawn |
    42	| First chart, 10,000 points | 34.0 ms | 28.4 ms | SVG lower |
    43	| 24-chart page at pixel ratio 2 | 199 ms | 158 ms | Void: no marks were drawn |
    44	| First chart, 3 × 120 | 23.6 ms | 19.8 ms | Inconclusive |
    45	| First chart, 100,000 points | 81.8 ms | 83.5 ms | Inconclusive |
    46	| First chart, 1,000,000 points | 622 ms | 652 ms | Inconclusive (4 blocks) |
    47	| Memory, 24-chart page at pixel ratio 2 | 34.2 MiB renderer, 11.5 MiB GPU, 7.7 MiB backing stores | 17.7 MiB, 2.2 MiB, none | Void: no marks were drawn |
    48	
    49	No frame was later than 25 ms in any configuration, so frame pacing does not separate the two.
    50	
    51	### Why SVG was the working default
    52	
    53	1. On the line workloads measured, main-thread task time was lower with SVG or the two could not be told apart.
    54	2. Line series are simplified to a few vertices per pixel column before either renderer sees them, so for line charts the path size follows the plot width, not the data.
    55	3. SVG follows the page with less code: forced colors and print work through CSS, browser zoom stays sharp, and there is no backing store to size, cap or lose. This is a design argument, not a measurement.
    56	
    57	### What M1 did not establish
    58	
    59	- **GPU rasterization was not measured.** Headless Chrome here does not use a GPU. The resize, pixel-ratio-2 and process-memory results need a headed, GPU-backed rerun before they transfer.
    60	- **Dense point marks were not measured.** A scatter chart with tens of thousands of markers is the case most likely to favour canvas.
    61	- **One browser, one machine, one session.** Firefox and Safari may order the two differently.
    62	- **Many series, pan and zoom, and the budget workloads P4, P7 and P8 were not measured**, and the million-point comparison has four pairs.
    63	- Both renderers are far from uPlot in the configurations measured (about 80 ms against 12 ms at 100,000 points; uPlot draws no tooltip or accessibility layer). Where that time goes is not established.

The adapters, screenshots and probe selectors are available for inspection. The keyboard walk starts at the first tab stop. The motion check compares two frames of bar entry. Container-cropped images cannot distinguish clipping from overflow. The study used no screen reader, touch device, other browser or customization task. [Adapters](../research/harness/src/libs/) · [Probe code](../research/harness/probe.mjs) · [Screenshots](../research/harness/shots/)

1	# Decision 0002: SVG draws the marks in 1.0
     2	
     3	Status: **final for 1.0**, confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-22. All shipped chart types draw marks with SVG. The benchmark harness retains the old Canvas records and can replay the renderer decision on the original sealed artifact.
     4	
     5	## Release evidence
     6	
     7	- The software family selected SVG under [rule 3](../04-plan-performance.md#51-declared-endpoints-provisional-until-the-pilot). Eight timing endpoints were too noisy to distinguish the renderers by the declared tolerances. Neither renderer had a late streaming run. The old Canvas implementation added 2,269 bytes gzipped in the matched script-tag measurement, above rule 3’s 512-byte cutoff. [Software decision](../../bench/decision/no-idle-2026-11-21/decision-renderer-20261121T143350Z.json)
     8	- The GPU family returned no decision because the dashboard GPU-memory result depended on run order. Canvas took less main-thread time on both GPU resize workloads beyond the tolerance, with neither difference reaching the worthwhile margin. [GPU decision](../../bench/decision/no-idle-2026-11-21/decision-gpu-20261121T143402Z.json)
     9	- Both families ran on Chrome 158.0.8127.36 on the same reference desktop, using artifact `20261119T091624Z-b643862f-b78698`. The owner accepted the 2026-11-21 measurements and dropped the idle-machine rule. Load is recorded with the results. [Benchmark method](../../bench/README.md)
    10	
    11	The SVG implementation uses CSS paint expressions for live theme changes and retains the plot's device-pixel geometry. 1.0 has no Canvas marks option. HTML text, accessibility, hit testing and streaming remain independent of the mark renderer.
    12	
    13	The matched packed consumer bundles shrank by 2,462 gzipped bytes for all chart types (118,252 to 115,790) and 1,628 for the line-only entry (98,627 to 96,999). The pair measures removal of the Canvas renderer, switch and Canvas-only styles with the shared renderer interface preserved. The SVG-only size snapshot uses artifact `20261122T055902Z-298b29e8-2e262a`, source hash `a57a243060881691`, before the startup optimizations. [Before removal](../../bench/results/size-before-svg-2026-11-22.json) · [After removal](../../bench/results/size-svg-contract-2026-11-22.json)
    14	
    15	## Historical M1 review and measurements
    16	
    17	The table below is kept as measured. These statements made from it in the first version are withdrawn or narrowed:
    18	
    19	- **Withdrawn: "nothing measured favours canvas except all-thread CPU during resize."** The recorded heap, DOM-node and layout counts also favour canvas.
    20	- **Withdrawn: the resize CPU gap is raster work.** The number is CPU for the whole renderer process; no stage was traced.
    21	- **Withdrawn: simplification bounds every chart by its width.** It was shown for line series only; point marks and many-series charts were not measured.
    22	- **Withdrawn: an SVG theme change needs no run-time work.** Both renderers recorded six DOM mutations per toggle; "no canvas drawing call" is all that was observed.
    23	- **Withdrawn: normalization and garbage collection explain the gap to uPlot.** About 71–73% of busy time in the production profiles is unmapped; the normalization share comes from development builds. It is a hypothesis to test, not a finding.
    24	- **Narrowed: "half the renderer memory."** The halving is of the increase above a data-only page at pixel ratio 2 (34.2 → 17.7 MiB). Absolute renderer memory was 74.7 → 56.2 MiB, and at pixel ratio 1 the increase was 23.1 → 18.4 MiB.
    25	- **Narrowed: "no frame later than 25 ms."** True of the recorded animation-frame callbacks; the window can miss an interval that spans its boundary, and a callback is not a presented frame.
    26	- **Void: every 24-chart page row** (page at pixel ratio 1 and 2, resize of the 24-chart page, and the memory row). The harness fix pass found that these runs drew no marks: at 230 × 115 px each tile is below the 120 × 80 px plot minimum of spec L8, so every chart showed its text fallback. The SVG records carry `svgPaths: 0`; the canvas runs held empty canvases. The numbers compare two empty charts and say nothing about the renderers. The harness now rejects a run whose chart drew no marks, and the page workload uses 340 × 200 px tiles.
    27	- **Narrowed: verdicts.** 149 metric comparisons were judged without adjustment for choosing among them, on six pairs or fewer per workload, with noise bands from one session and two workload shapes. Two "SVG lower" rows allow a gain as small as 0.16 ms (10,000 points) and 6.3 ms (dashboard at pixel ratio 2).
    28	
    29	Evidence: [bench/results/m1-renderer-comparison.md](../../bench/results/m1-renderer-comparison.md). One session of 39 runs, production build, headless Chrome 157, machine under load from other work, A-versus-A noise bands for two workloads only.
    30	
    31	### What M1 measured
    32	
    33	Canvas → SVG, medians of main-thread task time unless stated. "Lower" means the 95% interval cleared zero and the noise band where one existed.
    34	
    35	| Workload | Canvas | SVG | Verdict |
    36	|---|---|---|---|
    37	| Streaming, per update | 2.26 ms | 1.45 ms | SVG lower |
    38	| Theme change, per toggle | 2.68 ms and 27 drawing calls | 2.01 ms and no drawing call | SVG lower |
    39	| Resize, one chart of 100,000 points | 915 ms | 472 ms | SVG lower on the main thread |
    40	| Same, CPU across all threads | 1,035 ms | 1,770 ms | **SVG higher** |
    41	| Resize, 24-chart page | 730 ms | 525 ms | Void: no marks were drawn |
    42	| First chart, 10,000 points | 34.0 ms | 28.4 ms | SVG lower |
    43	| 24-chart page at pixel ratio 2 | 199 ms | 158 ms | Void: no marks were drawn |
    44	| First chart, 3 × 120 | 23.6 ms | 19.8 ms | Inconclusive |
    45	| First chart, 100,000 points | 81.8 ms | 83.5 ms | Inconclusive |
    46	| First chart, 1,000,000 points | 622 ms | 652 ms | Inconclusive (4 blocks) |
    47	| Memory, 24-chart page at pixel ratio 2 | 34.2 MiB renderer, 11.5 MiB GPU, 7.7 MiB backing stores | 17.7 MiB, 2.2 MiB, none | Void: no marks were drawn |
    48	
    49	No frame was later than 25 ms in any configuration, so frame pacing does not separate the two.
    50	
    51	### Why SVG was the working default
    52	
    53	1. On the line workloads measured, main-thread task time was lower with SVG or the two could not be told apart.
    54	2. Line series are simplified to a few vertices per pixel column before either renderer sees them, so for line charts the path size follows the plot width, not the data.
    55	3. SVG follows the page with less code: forced colors and print work through CSS, browser zoom stays sharp, and there is no backing store to size, cap or lose. This is a design argument, not a measurement.
    56	
    57	### What M1 did not establish
    58	
    59	- **GPU rasterization was not measured.** Headless Chrome here does not use a GPU. The resize, pixel-ratio-2 and process-memory results need a headed, GPU-backed rerun before they transfer.
    60	- **Dense point marks were not measured.** A scatter chart with tens of thousands of markers is the case most likely to favour canvas.
    61	- **One browser, one machine, one session.** Firefox and Safari may order the two differently.
    62	- **Many series, pan and zoom, and the budget workloads P4, P7 and P8 were not measured**, and the million-point comparison has four pairs.
    63	- Both renderers are far from uPlot in the configurations measured (about 80 ms against 12 ms at 100,000 points; uPlot draws no tooltip or accessibility layer). Where that time goes is not established.

docs/02-product-spec.md:257:## 6. Decisions and the findings behind them
   139	### 5.1 Declared endpoints (provisional until the pilot)
   140	
   141	Written on 2026-11-18, before any candidate was measured with the corrected harness, so that results cannot choose their own thresholds.
   142	
   143	**Per workload.** The primary metric is the one its budget names (spec section 5). The smallest worthwhile improvement is 10% of the budget's limit; the largest tolerated regression is 5% of it. Neither may be smaller than the upper edge of that workload's A-versus-A noise band: where the band is wider, the band is the threshold and the workload is listed as too noisy to gate at its nominal tolerance.
   144	
   145	| Budget | Workload in the harness | Primary metric | Smallest worthwhile | Tolerated regression |
   146	|---|---|---|---|---|
   147	| P1 | `first`, fixture `trend` | Task time, median over runs | 1 ms | 0.5 ms |
   148	| P2 | `first`, 1 × 100,000 | Same | 6 ms | 3 ms |
   149	| P2 | `first`, 1 × 1,000,000 | Same | 25 ms | 12.5 ms |
   150	| P3 | `stream`, window 600 | Task time per update: one value per run (task time in the window divided by updates), median over runs | 0.2 ms | 0.1 ms |
   151	| P3 | Same | Runs with any interval later than 25 ms | Fewer runs with late intervals | No more runs with late intervals than the baseline |
   152	| P4 | `hover`, 1 × 100,000 | Input to the frame showing the matching readout, 95th percentile per run, median over runs | 1.7 ms | 0.8 ms |
   153	| P5 | `page`, 24 tiles of 340 × 200 px, fixture `trend` | Total task time, median over runs | 20 ms | 10 ms |
   154	| P8 | `compact`, 40 tiles of 160 × 48 px, one series each | Same | 8 ms | 4 ms |
   155	| P7 | `mem`, 1 × 1,000,000 | Bytes owned beyond the caller's columns | 10% of the two columns | 5% of the two columns |
   156	| P7 | `lifecycle` | Heap after forced collection, cycles 1,500–2,000 against 2,000–2,500 | n/a | Growth above 1% between the two windows |
   157	
   158	**For the mark renderer (decision 0002).** Primary endpoints: P1, P2 at 100,000, P3 (both metrics), P5, P8, and three workloads that could reverse the choice: `scatter` at 50,000 points (first draw), `first` at 10 × 100,000, and `zoom` (task time per step at 1 × 100,000). The scatter, ten-series and zoom endpoints have no budget; their thresholds are 10% and 5% of the slower renderer's median in the pilot, fixed before the comparison runs. Because nine endpoints are judged together, each interval is computed at 99.4% (Bonferroni), not 95%.
   159	
   160	The rule, in order:
   161	1. A renderer that is worse beyond tolerance on any primary endpoint, and better beyond the smallest worthwhile improvement on none, loses.
   162	2. If each renderer wins somewhere, the default goes to the one that wins on more of P1, P3, P5 and P8 (the everyday cases), and the other is kept for the chart type where it wins only if its gain there is at least four times the smallest worthwhile improvement (section 5, "complexity is paid for").
   163	3. If nothing separates them, SVG stays and canvas is removed from the 1.0 bundle only if the size report shows it costs more than 0.5 KiB gzipped; otherwise both stay behind the switch.
   164	
   165	For rule 2, P3 counts as one everyday workload: a renderer wins it only if it is better on task time per update beyond the smallest worthwhile improvement and has no more runs with late intervals than the other; a renderer with more late runs loses it whatever its task time. If the two renderers win the same number of the four everyday workloads, rule 3 applies. A result is a verdict only when the session's A-versus-A control for that workload and those two builds, with at least 20 complete pairs in each of three sessions, puts the noise band below the threshold; otherwise the workload is "too noisy to gate" and counts for neither side. A pilot must show, for each endpoint, that the per-order (AB and BA) estimates agree within the noise band; where they do not, runs for that endpoint use a fresh browser process per run. A run that does not finish, or whose admission fails, is a failure of that renderer on that workload, not a missing value.
   166	
   167	How the harness reads these rules (`bench/src/decision.js`), accepted as part of the plan: a workload is too noisy when the noise edge reaches the tolerance; the noise edge is the larger of the two renderers' controls; an inconclusive primary endpoint blocks the decision and is rerun; if both renderers lose under rule 1 there is no decision yet; the late-interval endpoint of P3 compares counts of late runs, without an interval; the four-times retention test applies to measured intervals only; control sessions are separate A-versus-A jobs in the same environment as the comparison.
   168	
   169	On 2026-11-21 the owner dropped the idle-machine rule. In the owner's words, “pc under 10% usage is like not really used. stop with your crazy rules.” The one-minute load average at the start of every block is retained in the records for context only. A session must use one Chrome version. The owner also accepted the 2026-11-21 run as release evidence, saying “count it as release evvidence”.
   170	
   171	The GPU-dependent workloads (resize, pixel ratio 2, process memory) form a second family, "gpu", measured with Chrome rasterising on the machine's GPU (headless with `--enable-gpu --use-angle=gl --ignore-gpu-blocklist`, or headed), judged by the same rules with its own intervals: the 100,000-point resize (task time and late runs), the 24-chart resize, P1, P2 at 100,000 and P5 at pixel ratio 2, and the dashboard's renderer and GPU process memory at pixel ratio 2. Its everyday workloads for rule 2 are P1 and P5 at pixel ratio 2 and the two resizes; a resize is won as P3 is, with its task-time win and no more late runs. GPU and software sessions are different environments and never serve the same family. (An earlier version of this plan said this machine could not measure them; that was wrong: only the default headless mode renders in software.)
